registration.registered_before: any production FP8 or FP4 cell was collected

design.why_interleaved: the three floor64 launches ran consecutively inside one call, so their variance component is a WITHIN-SESSION one and a documented lower bound on what a differently-dated deployment launch would show. Interleaving the BF16 launches around the quantized collections makes any within-run drift land ON the launch factor instead of hiding underneath it. It cannot be removed -- launch identity and launch order are the same thing at R=3 -- so it is made conservative instead.

estimator.reported_headline: the locked single-reference mean of 64 per-trajectory means (analyze_kl.py, reference launch 1) -- unchanged
estimator.supplementary_estimand: E_r[KL(B_r || Q)], the divergence a randomly drawn BF16 launch of the locked profile exhibits
estimator.model: Y_{r,t} = mu + A_r + S_t + E_{rt}, Y = mean over the ten retained positions
estimator.launch_summary: F ratio and a one-sided 95% upper bound on sigma2_A, with the untruncated moment estimate beside them. At 2 df a truncated point estimate reports exactly 0.0 about 63% of the time under a null.
estimator.trajectory_summary: the pre-registered percentile bootstrap, unchanged in draws, seed, unit and shared index matrix
estimator.floor_treatment: reported beside, never subtracted; a spread, not a bias
estimator.fp8_fp4: measured directly with FP8 as reference; unchanged and carries no launch term

nuisance_model_prediction.predicted_quantity: SD of the three per-launch headlines, i.e. sqrt(sigma2_A + sigma2_E/T) -- NOT sigma_A
nuisance_model_prediction.falsified_if: the registered sigma_proj falls outside the 95% chi-square interval of the observed per-launch-headline SD, for both comparisons
nuisance_model_prediction.power_caveat: at R=3 that interval spans a factor of ~12. The test can embarrass the model but cannot confirm it, and this is stated before the run rather than after.

resolution_rule.applies_to: the BF16-anchored comparisons, at the headline and at every position
resolution_rule.rule: RESOLVED iff the lower end of the launch-inflated 95% interval on the signal exceeds the upper end of the 95% launch-level interval on the BF16<->BF16 replication floor, both evaluated at the same position
resolution_rule.signal_interval: the pre-registered percentile bootstrap interval, SCALED about the point estimate by sqrt(1 + var_launch/var_bootstrap). Scaled rather than rebuilt symmetrically: the percentile form was chosen for a right-skewed non-negative statistic and theta +/- z*SE can cross zero at the long positions.
resolution_rule.var_launch_per_position: from the pooled scaling law, var = (sigma_proj * sqrt(2*theta_p))^2. Per-position variance COMPONENTS are not estimable -- raw KL cells have kurtosis ~45, an effective df near 5% of nominal -- so the pooled coupling constant is what makes a per-position statement possible at all.
resolution_rule.sigma_proj_used: this run's own pooled estimate; the registered 2.1e-03 is applied as a stated sensitivity check, never as the primary
resolution_rule.floor_interval: delete-one-launch jackknife over the ordered pairs of THIS run's three BF16 launches; six ordered pairs are a U-statistic carrying R-1 = 2 df, not five
resolution_rule.no_position_is_dropped: classification is a label on a reported number. Positions are never selected, filtered or reordered by outcome, and the headline is computed over all ten regardless of class.
resolution_rule.why_not_post_hoc_selection: the rule is fixed here, before the FP8/FP4 cells exist. Which positions it lands on is data; the rule is not.

what_is_not_changed.G2_G2prime: recorded failures; thresholds unchanged; not re-adjudicated

locked_headline.definition: EVALUATION_RIG.md A.1: mean of per-trajectory means, single reference launch (launch 1). This is THE headline; everything else supplements.

vs_replication_floor.floor_rule: max over both sides of the pair

headline.interpretation: ratio is a reproducibility diagnostic only; read value_nats for magnitude. No materiality threshold is applied here.

worst_cell.interpretation: ratio is a reproducibility diagnostic only; read value_nats for magnitude. No materiality threshold is applied here.

vs_replication_floor.floor_rule: max over both sides of the pair

headline.interpretation: ratio is a reproducibility diagnostic only; read value_nats for magnitude. No materiality threshold is applied here.

worst_cell.interpretation: ratio is a reproducibility diagnostic only; read value_nats for magnitude. No materiality threshold is applied here.

marginal_step.why_no_launch_component: FP8 is the reference; no BF16 distribution enters it

larger_than_bf16_to_fp4.quantity: FP8||FP4 minus BF16||FP4, paired on the same 64 trajectories
larger_than_bf16_to_fp4.why_paired: the two marginal intervals overlap; the paired one is the interval the shared trajectories support
larger_than_bf16_to_fp4.not_a_divergence: a difference of two KLs is not a KL. This is a comparison of magnitudes and is never reported as the marginal step, which is the directly measured FP8||FP4.

marginal_step.matrix_sha256_note: SHA-256 of the exact float32 bytes consumed; the BF16 launches' digests are in launch_variance_p13.json

registered.predicted_quantity: SD of the three per-launch headlines, i.e. sqrt(sigma2_A + sigma2_E/T) -- NOT sigma_A
registered.falsified_if: the registered sigma_proj falls outside the 95% chi-square interval of the observed per-launch-headline SD, for both comparisons
registered.power_caveat: at R=3 that interval spans a factor of ~12. The test can embarrass the model but cannot confirm it, and this is stated before the run rather than after.

BF16||FP8.predicted_cv_registered_was_computed_at: the n=4 signal, not this run's

BF16||FP4.predicted_cv_registered_was_computed_at: the n=4 signal, not this run's

sharp_post_hoc_diagnostic.status: POST HOC -- not registered before the run; reported as a diagnostic, never as the adjudication
sharp_post_hoc_diagnostic.why_it_is_sharp: both SDs are functions of the same three launch perturbations, so the ratio carries far less sampling error than either SD alone
sharp_post_hoc_diagnostic.reading: the law says the ratio is sqrt(signal ratio); a ratio near 1 says the launch spread does not scale with the signal at all

pooled_observed.rule: root-mean-square over the BF16-anchored comparisons, equal weights
pooled_observed.why_pooled: sigma_proj is a property of the launch perturbation rather than of the configuration; agreement across configurations whose signals differ by nearly an order of magnitude is the evidence for pooling it

nuisance_model_prediction_test.verdict_is_weak_by_construction: the registered criterion is a CONJUNCTION over two arms computed from the SAME three BF16 launches, each tested against a chi-square interval spanning ~12x at 2 df. It is close to unfalsifiable as written. Read the verdict's own gloss and the pooled ratio rather than the label.

verdict_meaning.CONSISTENT: the registered sigma_proj sits inside the observed interval for every comparison. At 2 df that interval spans a factor of ~12, so this is a failure to embarrass the model, not a confirmation of it.
verdict_meaning.FALSIFIED: the registered value is outside the observed interval for every comparison; the nuisance model as registered is wrong
verdict_meaning.MIXED: the comparisons disagree; the pooled coupling constant is not supported

BF16||FP8.rule: RESOLVED iff the lower end of the launch-inflated 95% interval on the signal exceeds the upper end of the 95% launch-level interval on the BF16<->BF16 replication floor, both evaluated at the same position
BF16||FP8.what_resolved_licenses: the estimated divergence at this position, after trajectory-sampling uncertainty and the registered launch inflation, exceeds the upper launch-level bound on the typical BF16<->BF16 divergence. It does NOT license 'separable from relaunch noise': the floor is SECOND order in the launch perturbation while the signal is FIRST order, so the floor is not the noise the signal is exposed to. Separability from relaunch noise would be theta against its own SD_launch, against which every position clears by one to three orders of magnitude.
BF16||FP8.what_noise_limited_means: this rig cannot put the position's divergence above the floor's upper launch bound. It is a statement about resolution, not about the effect being absent, and the position still contributes to the headline. Read `binding_uncertainty` before attributing it to launch noise -- where the inflation factor is ~1.00 the limit is trajectory sampling, not relaunching.
BF16||FP8.multiplicity: no multiplicity correction is applied and none is implied. The ten positions are repeated measures on the same 64 trajectories sharing one bootstrap index matrix, so they are strongly dependent and must not be read as ten independent tests.
BF16||FP8.floor_side_uncertainty_is_launch_only: floor_hi covers launch sampling (delete-one-launch jackknife, 2 df) and not the floor's own trajectory sampling. Carrying both would widen floor_hi; see floor_side_sensitivity.

resolution_rule_conservatism.registered_var_launch: (sigma_proj * sqrt(2*theta))^2, i.e. the variance of the SPREAD OF PER-LAUNCH HEADLINES, sigma2_A + sigma2_E/T
resolution_rule_conservatism.what_a_ci_on_the_mean_would_use: sigma2_A / R -- the launch term of Var(mean over R launches). sigma2_E/(R*T) is already inside the trajectory bootstrap, so the registered form double-counts it and omits the 1/R.
resolution_rule_conservatism.direction: CONSERVATIVE -- the registered form is larger, so it widens the interval and makes `resolved` harder to reach
resolution_rule_conservatism.not_corrected_because: the formula is what was registered before the FP8/FP4 cells existed, and the correction runs in the resolution-friendly direction. Changing it after seeing the data is exactly what pre-registration exists to prevent. It is disclosed instead.
resolution_rule_conservatism.magnitude: immaterial here: inflation factors span [1.0001, 1.0081] and no classification depends on the launch term

floor_side_sensitivity.question: does carrying the floor's own trajectory-sampling uncertainty change any classification?
floor_side_sensitivity.method: floor_hi recomputed as mean + t(df) * sqrt(se_jackknife^2 + se_trajectory^2); the floor's trajectory SE is a single pooled figure, so this is indicative
floor_side_sensitivity.not_adopted: the registered rule is what adjudicates; this is a sensitivity check and is reported beside it, never in place of it

G2_G2prime.status: RECORDED FAILURES; unchanged by this run

primary_floor.which: the PRE-REGISTERED production floor, the denominator G2' was adjudicated against

this_run_floor.which: this run's own BF16<->BF16 mean over six ordered pairs of its three launches

move_from_the_smoke_figure.reading: the fall from the smoke figure is mostly the signal -- the production BF16->FP8 KL is larger than the n=4 estimate -- but NOT entirely: part of it is a smaller floor in this run. Both floors are within each other's launch-level intervals, so the difference is not itself resolvable.

G2_G2prime.conclusion: G2' fails on every floor/signal combination in this run's artifacts. The bound is unchanged at 0.01 and no result was averaged or re-referenced.
G2_G2prime.floor_not_applicable_because: the BF16 replication floor bounds BF16-anchored comparisons. FP8||FP4 uses FP8 as its reference, whose own replication floor is ~1e-11 nats.
